title: Extracting Quantitative 3D Nano-Scale Structure and Strain From Diffraction-Contrast TEM Images Using Machine Learning
content: Image contrast due to electron diffraction in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) is highly sensitive to sample geometry, crystal lattice distortion, and even minute deviations from Bragg condition [1]. However, although this means diffraction-contrast micrographs encode a wealth of nanometer-scale structure and strain information, direct interpretation of this contrast is difficult and non-intuitive, particularly for complex 3D structures and defect arrangements. The conventional approach, involving “pattern matching” experimental images with those simulated from a “best guess” of the underlying structure, is laborious and limited, only scratching the surface of the information locked within. Such measurements are important since strains generated from crystal defects, such as dislocations and point-defect clusters, strongly affect the electronic, mechanical, and transport behavior of all crystalline materials. Various advanced techniques have been developed for measuring local strain – such as geometric phase analysis, 4D-STEM, or Bragg coherent diffraction imaging – While powerful, these are all limited either to 2D, specific orientations, and/or low spatial resolutions. Instead, we leverage machine learning (ML) to recast the measurement of the nanoscale 3D structure and strain fields/tensors as a computational imaging inverse problem.
